lead: >-
  "Amazing Salta" is a 5-day journey through northwestern Argentina featuring Cafayate wineries, Los Cardones National Park, settlements in Quebrada de Humahuaca, and the Salinas Grandes salt flats. The itinerary involves several lengthy drives and changing mountain landscapes. Discover how each stage differs, which excursions are included, and which expenses need to be budgeted separately.
---

## Salta in 5 days: an itinerary through wine valleys and the Andes

This tour introduces three distinct aspects of northwestern Argentina. Around [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/), the focus is on vineyards and winemaking. On the road through [Los Cardones](/argentina/place/los-cardones-national-park/), mountain scenery and towering cacti take center stage. Farther north in [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/), the route passes settlements where natural formations are closely intertwined with history and local traditions.

[Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) serves as both the starting and finishing point. The journey is not limited to daily city strolls: it includes overnight stops along the route, mountain roads through the Andes, and visits to several widely separated areas.

## Why does the first part focus on Cafayate?

At the beginning of the trip, the group travels to Cafayate, a drive of approximately 3 hours after arriving in Salta. This wine-growing district features a visit to a winery, where a guide explains grape cultivation, winemaking, and aging. There is also free time in town and a visit to the wine museum.

The itinerary includes a night at a wine hotel. This means more time to discover the region than a brief stop at a winery en route to another town. However, **lunch in Cafayate's central square is paid for separately**. Evaluate the wine portion according to the specifically confirmed visits rather than assuming every tasting and meal is included.

For a holiday entirely dedicated to winemaking, also compare [food and wine tours in Argentina](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/). On "Amazing Salta," wine is one of several major experiences.

## Los Cardones and Quebrada de Humahuaca: two different mountain landscapes

The return drive toward Salta includes [Los Cardones National Park](/argentina/place/los-cardones-national-park/), with its tall cacti and scenic stops. The itinerary particularly mentions old cactus specimens and the opportunity to hear legends associated with the area.

The journey then continues toward [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and the famous Hill of Seven Colors. An important part of this stage is [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/), a UNESCO-listed cultural landscape. Its value lies not only in its colorful slopes but also in the surviving history of trading routes and settlements from different eras.

In [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/), the route introduces an ancient fortified settlement; in [Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/), a historic church and religious art; and in [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/), old streets and monuments from the colonial period. Together, these stops form the cultural portion of the journey, easily overlooked if you focus only on photographs of colorful mountains.

## Salinas Grandes: why allow plenty of time for the salt flats?

From Purmamarca, the route leads to [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/) before returning to Salta. The salt flats' white surface and exposed high-altitude terrain contrast sharply with Cafayate's vineyards and the green Lerma Valley.

This is one of the itinerary's longest driving stages. The road, stops, and weather conditions affect the actual duration of the day. Treat the salt flats as a full excursion, not a quick break on the way to the airport.

High-altitude areas can be cold and windy even when Salta is warm. Comfortable shoes for uneven ground, warm outerwear, and sun protection will help. If you find altitude difficult, discuss the route and physical demands before traveling.

## Transfers and overnight stays: judging the pace

| Day | Main area |
|---|---|
| 1 | Salta and Cafayate |
| 2 | Los Cardones, return to Salta |
| 3 | Purmamarca and Humahuaca Valley |
| 4 | Salinas Grandes, return to Salta |
| 5 | Departure from Salta |

The description estimates the drive from Salta to Purmamarca at around 4 hours; returning from the salt flats also involves a long journey. Consider not only the total number of days but how much time remains for walking, photography, and rest. This itinerary is better suited to travelers who enjoy a busy sightseeing program than to those who want several days in one hotel.

## What is included, and what costs extra?

The price includes hotel accommodation, meals specified in the itinerary, private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, and chauffeured transfers. International and domestic flights, additional food and drinks, other excursions, tips, and laundry are listed separately. Accommodation may be substituted with hotels of the same category.

The domestic flight to Salta deserves special attention: the land itinerary starts after arrival in the city, but domestic flights are not included in the tour price. Confirm the airport and pickup time when choosing flights, so the three-hour drive to Cafayate does not extend too far into the evening.

Read more about the country, its regions, and seasons in our [Argentina travel guide](/argentina/). To compare other ready-made itineraries, see [all Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the "Amazing Salta" tour

### Can I see the salt flats and the Hill of Seven Colors on one trip?

Yes. This program includes [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/) on different excursion stages of the same five-day journey.

### Is the tour mainly about wine?

No. The Cafayate wineries feature in the first part of the itinerary. The national park, historic settlements, multicolored mountains, and salt flats follow.

### Are domestic flight tickets included?

No. Domestic and international flights are listed among the expenses paid separately. Coordinate your arrival in Salta with the start of the sightseeing program.

### Do I need to prepare for altitude?

The itinerary passes through high-altitude areas and involves lengthy drives. If you have medical conditions or concerns about how you tolerate altitude, discuss participation with your doctor and the tour organizer in advance. This is a sightseeing itinerary, not a mountain summit climb.

## Bariloche and Buenos Aires in 6 days: Andean lakes and the capital

The [Bariloche and Buenos Aires tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-bariloche-buenos-aires/) lasts **6 days and 5 nights**. The first two nights are spent in [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), among Andean lakes and mountains, and the next three in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), with its distinctive neighborhoods, architecture, and tango.

This itinerary introduces two very different sides of Argentina without covering numerous natural regions. Unlike longer journeys through Patagonia, Iguazú, and the northwest, it involves only one main flight between cities. Even so, part of the six calendar days is spent in transit.

## Bariloche: why is the Circuito Chico route important?

A *Circuito Chico* excursion around Bariloche is scheduled for the second day. The road follows Bustillo Avenue beside [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/), passes [Playa Bonita](/argentina/place/playa-bonita/), and leads to beautiful views of the Llao Llao peninsula, Lake Moreno, and nearby mountain ranges.

The main viewpoint is [Cerro Campanario](/argentina/place/cerro-campanario/). The ascent to its lookout is expressly listed among the included services. From above, lakes, peninsulas, forests, and mountains spread out below, showing why Bariloche is so popular for scenic road excursions.

Bariloche's official tourism portal describes Circuito Chico as a classic local excursion taking several hours. Our itinerary leaves free time after the scenic circuit, and no long, demanding mountain trek is mandatory.

| Day | Highlight |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival in Bariloche |
| 2 | Circuito Chico |
| 3 | Flight to Buenos Aires |
| 4 | City sightseeing and tango show |
| 5 | Free time |
| 6 | Flight home |

## Buenos Aires: what can you see in three nights?

Day 3 includes transfer to Bariloche airport, a flight to the capital, a welcome on arrival, and a private transfer to the selected hotel. The rest of the day is free. This is not a full sightseeing day, as the arrival time depends on the flight.

On day 4, the tour introduces major areas of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): Plaza de Mayo, La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta, Palermo, and Puerto Madero. This overview combines historic squares, old immigrant neighborhoods, and the modern city.

The evening includes dinner and a tango show at **La Ventana Barrio de Tango**. This is not presented as an optional extra: the evening experience is explicitly named among the inclusions. Day 5 is free for independent exploration or additional excursions, which are paid for under separate terms.

## What is included, and what should be confirmed?

The price includes 2 nights in Bariloche and 3 in Buenos Aires, breakfasts, the Circuito Chico excursion, **the ascent to Cerro Campanario**, Buenos Aires sightseeing, dinner with a tango show, and transfers.

The transport arrangements vary: **scheduled/shared transfers** are provided in Bariloche, while transfers in Buenos Aires are **private**. Travelers requiring a private car for every stage should discuss this distinction before booking.

International flights, optional excursions, and the ecotourism tax in both cities are excluded. **The Bariloche–Buenos Aires flight appears in the daily itinerary but is not listed separately among the included services.** Confirm whether the airfare is part of your quoted rate in the final calculation; it would be misleading to assume its inclusion from the day description.

Find the detailed rates and conditions on the [six-day tour page](/argentina/tour/argentina-bariloche-buenos-aires/).

## Climate, clothing, and the best season

Bariloche's weather varies with elevation, wind, and season. The lakes region offers scenic drives year-round, but road conditions, lift operations, and possible maintenance closures should be checked for the intended date. Nonslip shoes and wind protection are advisable at viewpoints.

Buenos Aires has a more urban itinerary. Comfortable shoes and ordinary city clothing work well for the historic neighborhoods and evening tango. A single trip therefore requires clothing suitable for both mountain lakes and city evenings.

Traveling between the cities occupies a substantial portion of day 3. Avoid adding another complicated excursion to that day when selecting flights; there is already a dedicated free day in the capital.

## What other itineraries should you compare?

Travelers who also want to see [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), Tierra del Fuego, and the waterfalls can consider the [14-day Argentina–Patagonia–Iguazú tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/). It includes Bariloche as part of a longer journey with more flights and changes of climate.

The [15-day program with Mendoza and Salta](/argentina/tour/argentina-patagonia-highlights-2024/) focuses on wineries and the northwest; it is not simply a more complete version of the six-day tour. Use the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/) and [Bariloche guide](/argentina/place/bariloche/) to compare durations and regions.

## Frequently asked questions about Bariloche–Buenos Aires

### How many nights are spent in each city?

Two nights in Bariloche and three in Buenos Aires. The trip covers 6 calendar days in total.

### Is the Cerro Campanario ascent included?

Yes. It is expressly listed among the tour's included services.

### Are dinner and the tango show included?

Yes. Dinner and a performance at La Ventana are scheduled on day 4 in Buenos Aires.

### Is the domestic airfare included?

The flight appears in the daily schedule but is not separately specified in the list of included services. **Its cost must be confirmed in the final quote.**

### Will we see Perito Moreno?

No. The six-day itinerary covers only Bariloche and Buenos Aires. A different tour is required to visit [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/).

## 15 days from Patagonia's glaciers to the highlands and Iguazú

This **15-day, 14-night** itinerary includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and Perito Moreno Glacier, the [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) region, and Iguazú Falls. Each area differs greatly from the next, making this journey a good choice for travelers who want to experience several natural and cultural sides of Argentina in one trip.

Comfortable travel depends above all on preparing for domestic flights and changing temperatures and elevations. The itinerary suits people who enjoy extended sightseeing journeys rather than relaxing in the same hotel throughout.

## Buenos Aires and tango: a cultural beginning

The first days focus on [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): the historic districts of La Boca and San Telmo, central avenues, Recoleta, and other neighborhoods. The program includes an evening tango performance with dinner and transfers.

It is important to distinguish the guiding arrangements. No separate guide is provided at the evening show; it is a cultural performance, unlike the city's sightseeing excursion. After the city program, there is a free day for rest or independent exploration.

## Perito Moreno: viewing platforms and a boat trip

From the capital you fly to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). The excursion to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/) includes a walk along viewing paths and a **one-hour Safari Náutico cruise on a shared boat**.

These are two ways to see the glacier's ice front: from land, with different levels of viewing platforms, and from the water. The glacier changes continually, but the calving of large chunks of ice cannot be guaranteed at a particular time.

Warm, wind-resistant clothing is essential for this stage. Even if your trip continues to warmer parts of the country, conditions around Patagonia's glaciers may be cold and windy. A free day in El Calafate follows the excursion.

## Salta, Purmamarca, and Salinas Grandes: high-altitude conditions

The itinerary then passes through [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/), [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and the Hill of Seven Colors, [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/), and the [Salinas Grandes salt flats](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/). UNESCO recognizes Quebrada de Humahuaca as a cultural landscape associated with ancient trade routes and the history of Andean settlements.

This stage reveals red and multicolored rock formations, settlements with colonial architecture, and vast salt flats. These areas are much higher than Buenos Aires, and mountain roads can experience sudden weather changes.

People with medical conditions sensitive to altitude should discuss the suitability of the highlands with a doctor before traveling. For other travelers, water, sun protection, and warm clothes against the wind are helpful. This is not a technical mountaineering expedition, but the altitude and drives require attention.

## Both sides of Iguazú at the end of the itinerary

The final nature-focused stage includes the [Argentine side of Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the [Brazilian side near Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). They are scheduled on separate days: Argentina's walkways bring you close to individual cascades, while the Brazilian side offers a broad panorama.

Access to particular walkways, including the Devil's Throat area, sometimes changes with river conditions. Check whether each location is open for your travel dates. In addition, **visiting Brazil involves a real international border crossing**, even though Argentina is the tour's main country. Entry requirements depend on each traveler's nationality, not the package name.

## What is included, and what costs remain?

The tour price includes **4–5-star hotels with breakfast**, private transfers with a driver only, private excursions with **English-speaking guides**, and national park admission tickets. The evening tango show and excursions are described in the program; other optional activities are arranged separately.

The tour price is **$5375**. **Domestic and international air tickets are not included.** Domestic flight costs are calculated separately, and actual fares and schedules depend on the travel date, so they must be confirmed when preparing the quote. Tips, additional excursions, early check-in, and late check-out are also excluded.

With frequent flights, leave sufficient time for connections and coordinate baggage arrangements. The route moves between humid tropics, Patagonia's cold, and high-altitude areas. Packing in layers is practical, with light clothes for Iguazú and wind protection for El Calafate and Salta.

## How it differs from nearby itineraries

If you want to keep the glacier and Iguazú but replace the northwest highlands with wineries, compare the [12-day tour through Mendoza](/argentina/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-mendoza-el-calafate-iguazu/). If geological parks and Atlantic wildlife appeal more, consider the [13-day prehistoric journey](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/). Other options are listed in the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 15-day tour

### Does the program include Perito Moreno Glacier?

Yes. Viewing platforms and a Safari Náutico boat trip on a shared vessel are scheduled.

### Do I need to prepare for the altitude around Salta?

Visits to high-altitude settlements and salt flats require consideration of elevation. Travelers with relevant medical restrictions should discuss the itinerary with their doctor before departure.

### Are both sides of the waterfalls included?

Yes. The Argentine and Brazilian sides of Iguazú are scheduled on separate days. Some walkways may be temporarily closed.

### Are domestic flights and a Russian-speaking guide included?

No. Flights are paid for separately, and the included private excursions are described as English-speaking.

## How the Buenos Aires–Mendoza–glacier–Iguazú tour works

Over **12 days and 11 nights**, the program combines [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), and both sides of Iguazú Falls. It is suitable for a first extended exploration of Argentina if you want to see the capital, Andean vineyards, glacial Patagonia, and subtropical forests on one journey.

An important feature is the need for several domestic flights and changes of climatic region. Accommodation and guiding arrangements differ between stages. It would therefore be misleading to compare this program with a short tour of a single province on price alone.

## Why is a full day devoted to Mendoza's wineries?

Travelers fly from Buenos Aires to [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/). Here the main experience is an excursion through the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/), including **3 wineries**, tastings, and lunch at one of them. A specialist wine guide explains grape cultivation, the local climate, and the characteristics of Malbec.

This day is well suited to people for whom wine culture is a destination in itself. The stops form a planned sequence, not a quick tasting en route. If winemaking is your primary interest, compare [Argentina's food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/); on this journey, very different natural experiences follow Mendoza.

## What to expect at Perito Moreno Glacier

The next stage runs from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The main excursion focuses on observing the ice front from viewing platforms and maintained paths.

Ice may break off into the lake at any moment. It is a natural process with no timetable, so neither the guide nor the tour operator can guarantee a particular spectacle. Ordinary visits can be enjoyed from authorized walkways.

**Ice trekking for $360 per person** is offered separately. Do not confuse it with the main excursion: walking on the glacier itself requires separate authorization, equipment, and consideration of physical demands. If this is a priority, confirm the terms in advance.

## Both sides of Iguazú Falls

After Patagonia, the journey continues to [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Two separate days are allocated to the waterfalls. Argentina's walkways bring travelers close to the cascades, while Brazil offers wide panoramas.

On the Brazilian side, additional options may include the Bird Park for **$50** or a helicopter flight for **$170 per person**. These are optional expenses, not compulsory parts of the waterfall day.

Although **Argentina is the tour's main country**, the itinerary includes an actual visit to Brazil. Border entry requirements must therefore be checked in advance for each traveler's nationality. Individual park walkways may also become unavailable, for example because of high water levels.

## Transport, guides, and accommodation

The price includes **4-star hotel accommodation with breakfasts**, private chauffeured transfers, guided excursions, and admissions specified in the program. The language and format of guiding, however, differ:

| Region | Guiding |
| --- | --- |
| Buenos Aires and Iguazú | Private, in Russian |
| Mendoza | English-speaking guide |
| El Calafate | Group excursion, in English |

Flights connect the regions. The trip from El Calafate to Iguazú involves a connection in Buenos Aires. **International and domestic air tickets are excluded from the tour price.** Leave sufficient time for such connections and plan flights together with excursion days.

Buenos Aires includes a free day. Paid options include a trip to [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) for $100, a "Gaucho Fiesta" for $250, or an excursion to Montevideo. **Uruguay is only an optional destination**, not a mandatory country on the itinerary.

## What to pack for different climatic zones

Comfortable city clothing is useful for Mendoza and Buenos Aires, while Patagonia requires protection against cold and wind. On Iguazú's tropical trails, nonslip footwear and waterproof layers are helpful: spray from the cascades can soak clothes even without rain. Temperatures vary by season and differ considerably among these regions.

The base program price is **$3213**. Air tickets, optional excursions, tips, early check-in, late check-out, and personal expenses are extra. Specific accommodation arrangements are confirmed when agreeing the trip.

To compare the northwest of Argentina with the wine itinerary, see the [15-day tour through Salta, El Calafate, and Iguazú](/argentina/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-el-calafate-salta-iguazu/) and other [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Mendoza–El Calafate–Iguazú route

### Does the tour include both sides of Iguazú?

Yes. Separate excursions on the Argentine and Brazilian sides are scheduled on different days; actual access to some trails depends on park conditions.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide on every stage?

No. Russian-language guiding is provided in Buenos Aires and Iguazú; Mendoza and El Calafate use English-speaking guides.

### Is trekking on the glacier itself included?

No. Perito Moreno ice trekking is an optional service costing $360 per person.

### Do domestic air tickets need to be purchased separately?

Yes. International and domestic flights are listed as expenses outside the package price.

## Corporate tour in Buenos Aires: combining business with exploring Argentina

This program suits a group whose business activities take place in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and whose members want to discover the city afterward. The itinerary includes three days with congress sessions, cultural activities, and a separate visit to [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/). There is no need for a series of flights between regions: most of the stay is in the capital and its surroundings.

Unlike organizing an independent corporate event, this tour provides a specific **travel and sightseeing program around the congress**. The congress's technical support, room hire, equipment, and speaker arrangements should not be assumed to be included without a separate agreement. For broader business travel needs, explore [business delegation trips](/mice/business-delegations/).

## How working time fits into the five days

On arrival, the group is met at the airport and accompanied to the hotel. Days 2, 3, and 4 contain business sessions, followed by different activities.

| Stage | Main activity |
|---|---|
| Arrival day | Hotel check-in and welcome dinner |
| Day 2 | Congress, city tour, tango |
| Day 3 | Congress and trip to Tigre |
| Day 4 | Congress and group dinner |
| Departure day | Breakfast and airport transfer |

The city sightseeing day includes a separate four-hour excursion. Agree on the end time of the meetings in advance: this leaves time for Plaza de Mayo, San Telmo, La Boca, Recoleta, and Puerto Madero without an overly tight schedule. The evening tango show also requires travel time and seating arrangements.

No substantial standalone excursion is planned for day 4. This is helpful if the congress involves a lengthy working session. Avoid filling the day with extra activities automatically; first establish the host group's objectives and meeting schedule.

## Why Tigre is a separate excursion

[Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) lies north of Buenos Aires and is known for the waterways of the Paraná Delta. For congress participants, it offers a change from city streets to islands, water, and waterfront houses. The program schedules a trip after the morning business session and **a private boat outing**.

This is an important detail: the private boat is explicitly included in the described itinerary and can be taken into account when discussing the route. However, the vessel's capacity, seating layout, length of stops, and suitability for holding a separate event on board are not specified. These questions should be resolved according to the size of the corporate group.

A local market and an art museum are also mentioned in Tigre. Distinguish the exact form of any visit from the boat outing: an attraction's appearance in the itinerary does not itself guarantee a separate guided museum tour with admission included.

## Transfers, hotel, and evening activities

We offer accommodation at Palladium Buenos Aires, a meeting with a guide at the international airport, transfers along the itinerary, and guides for excursions. Ada Tours reserves the option to substitute another hotel of the same category. When confirming the trip, specify room types, group composition, and arrival schedules for different flights.

The itinerary names La Cabaña, Piegari Carnes, and Fervor restaurants, and Michelangelo Tango for the tango evening. These venues illustrate the intended character of gatherings after the congress. But listing them **does not automatically establish** that any selected menu, drinks, and every dinner are included in a single group rate. The commercial proposal should itemize such arrangements.

For a relaxed evening, coordinate the end of business meetings, hotel departure, show start time, and return of the group. If participants are accommodated at several hotels, separate pickup arrangements will be necessary.

## How to check the terms of a group proposal

This tour does not yet have one confirmed price per person or for the entire group. Comparing it with a private sightseeing tour on an assumed "from" price would therefore be misleading. The final quote depends primarily on the number of participants, selected room types, and the agreed activities.

Before approving the budget, compare 5 core items: accommodation with breakfasts; airport and city transfers; guide services; admissions for scheduled visits; and restaurants and evening events with specific menus. International flights, extra excursions, and tips are listed separately as exclusions.

If participants come from different countries, collect their flight schedules and preferred guiding languages in advance. The mention of a guide in the description does not automatically specify the language of every presentation, tour, or business meeting.

Other options by duration and geography can be found in the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/). For this itinerary, the decisive factor is how well the congress schedule fits with cultural activities, not the number of sights packed into one day.

## Frequently asked questions about the Buenos Aires and Tigre corporate trip

### Is the congress included in the tour price as an organized event?

The itinerary reserves time for a congress but does not provide a separate confirmed list covering venue hire, equipment, or organization of the event itself. These services must be agreed separately.

### What do participants do in Tigre?

After the morning business session, they travel to the [Paraná Delta near Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) and take a private boat outing. A market and museum are also mentioned; the exact format of those visits should be clarified.

### How many nights does the program last?

The plan covers 5 days and 4 nights, with arrival on day 1 and departure on day 5. Exact flights and any additional accommodation are coordinated for the group.

### Are all restaurants and the tango show included in the overall budget?

The evening venues are named in the itinerary, but there is no universal itemization of each menu and its cost. The final proposal must explicitly confirm what is included for your group.
